newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks end with minor gains, narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks end with minor gains, narrow range.

text.p: Bombay blue chips notched small gains in sluggish trade on Friday as major players kept to the sidelines in the absence of a clear market trend, dealers said.

"The index was traded around the same levels today. The undertone remains strong...we haven't seen much of a downtrend in many stocks," said Yogendra Shah, director at YSN Shares Pvt Ltd, a domestic firm.
Dealers said subdued speculative activity left the market becalmed. Much of the action was focussed on scattered foreign fund buying seen in pivotal stocks, they said.

"There was some buying interest by foreign funds in select shares such as Arvind Mills, Dr Reddy's Laboratories, Bombay Suburban Electric Supply and Tata Engineering & Locomotive Company (TELCO)," said a chief dealer at a local securities house.
"Valuations are quite attractive and that is perhaps inducing the buying interest in these shares," he added.
Dealers said the undertone remained firm and speculators displayed hesitancy to go short on front-bencher stocks at current prices.
"People are hoping for a good budget and some positive announcements. The market's technical position is good, buyers are taking deliveries of stocks," YSN's Shah said.

The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top 30-share index finished with a net gain of 30.16 points, to a provisional 3,522.81, off its intra-day high of 3,528.56. The National Stock Exchange index was up 9.35 points, or 0.93 percent, to 1,001.50.
At the BSE, bank stock State Bank of India jumped 9.75 rupees, or 3.51 percent, to 287.25, topping the list of market outperformers. Reliance Industries rose 1.75 to 273.50 and TELCO 10.0 to 342.50.
